s1.syndrome_frame: Rectal ulcer with a history of radiation therapy
salient_findings: Large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall
key_facts: 57-year-old man
Asymptomatic
History of stage IIIc localized prostate cancer
Completed a course of prostate-directed radiation therapy with a SpaceOAR hydrogel spacer
Mild straining with bowel movements
Occasional passage of mucus
Large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall
Firm margins, friability, and exudate
Biopsies of the lesion were negative for malignancy
Spacer positioned between the prostate and rectum

shortlist.label: Radiation proctitis
shortlist.why_kept: History of prostate-directed radiation therapy and presence of a large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall

shortlist.label: Solitary rectal ulcer syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall with firm margins, friability, and exudate

shortlist.label: Rectal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: History of stage IIIc localized prostate cancer and presence of a large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall, although biopsies were negative for malignancy

shortlist.label: Prostate cancer metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of stage IIIc localized prostate cancer and presence of a large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall, although biopsies were negative for malignancy

shortlist.label: Ulcerative colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of a large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall with friability and exudate, although the remainder of the rectum appeared normal

raw.rationale: The patient's history of prostate-directed radiation therapy and the presence of a large deep-cratered solitary ulcer on the anterior rectal wall, which is a common site for radiation injury, support this diagnosis. The biopsies being negative for malignancy also rule out rectal cancer and prostate cancer metastasis, making radiation proctitis the most likely explanation for the patient's symptoms and findings.

rejected.label: Solitary rectal ulcer syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has a solitary ulcer, the history of radiation therapy and the location of the ulcer on the anterior rectal wall are more consistent with radiation proctitis.

rejected.label: Rectal cancer
rejected.why: Biopsies of the lesion were negative for malignancy, ruling out rectal cancer.

rejected.label: Prostate cancer metastasis
rejected.why: Biopsies of the lesion were negative for malignancy, and the patient's prostate cancer was localized, making metastasis less likely.

rejected.label: Ulcerative colitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and colonoscopy findings are not consistent with ulcerative colitis, which typically presents with diffuse inflammation and ulceration throughout the colon.
